newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi confirms deals for over 1.4 mln T barley.
newsitem.headline: Saudi confirms deals for over 1.4 mln T barley.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has confirmed it signed deals to buy more than 1.4 million tonnes of barley, the official Saudi Press Agency reported late on Sunday.

It quoted Agriculture and Water Minister Abdullah bin Abdul-Aziz bin Muammar as saying the state Grain Silos and Flour Mills Organisation had signed the deals, which would help meet growing local demand.

"The minister revealed that contracts had been finalised to buy a new additional amount of barley at the beginning of this week of more than 1.4 million tonnes to cover needs over the coming months," SPA said.
He did not say where the barley would be sourced or when it would be delivered.
Industry sources had said Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest buyer of feed barley, last week bought the barley for import between October and December.
Dealers said the purchase was made at prices ranging from $146 to $158 per tonne, including cost and freight.
Muammar said barley sales within the kingdom in the Islamic month, which began in mid-August, were around 469,000 tonnes from 420,000 tonnes in the month to mid-June.
